purpose: Migrates the plugin's preconnect/dns-prefetch hint emission from a raw wp_head echo path to WordPress core's wp_resource_hints() filter, gaining core's deduplication, normalization, and cross-plugin interoperability while preserving the crossorigin="anonymous" attribute on preconnect hints.
riskRationale: The migration is architecturally sound and lint/tests pass, but core's wp_resource_hints() silently discards URLs that parse without a host, which drops bare-hostname DNS-prefetch entries (e.g. "example.com", the exact format the settings UI placeholder recommends) — a silent functional regression. Rendered output also normalizes (protocol-relative dns-prefetch, scheme+host preconnect), so it is not byte-identical to the legacy output despite the docblock's claim.

text: Well-scoped migration to core's wp_resource_hints() filter with clean append semantics ($urls[] / array_merge), correct preservation of the crossorigin attribute, graceful handling of disabled/missing settings, and solid unit tests covering the method's branches. The main gap is that origins entered as bare hostnames (the DNS-prefetch UI's documented input format) are silently dropped by core's host-less URL guard, and the tests — which exercise the method in isolation rather than core's render path — fail to catch this.

reasoning: The migration itself is correct, but the dns-prefetch branch drops bare-hostname origins (e.g. "example.com", the format shown in the PreloadSettings textarea placeholder), silently disabling DNS-prefetch for any site that followed the documented input format. Normalizing scheme-less origins to protocol-relative form before returning fixes this with a small, safe change.

message: Correct append semantics: preconnect uses $urls[] and dns-prefetch uses array_merge(), so other plugins' existing hints are never clobbered, and the callback returns $urls unchanged for unrelated relation types (prefetch/prerender) and for disabled or missing settings.
Preserving the crossorigin="anonymous" attribute via the array-hint format is the right way to keep the legacy preconnect semantics through core's filter.

The reflection-based make_main() helper follows the existing BlockAssetsFiltersTest.php convention, and the test matrix (enabled/disabled/missing settings, unrelated relation types) is good branch coverage of the method.

Bare-hostname dns-prefetch origins are silently dropped. Core's wp_resource_hints() skips any URL where wp_parse_url() yields no host (parse_url('example.com') returns only a 'path'), and this is exactly the input format the settings UI documents: PreloadSettings.js line 263 uses placeholder="example.com". Previously the legacy echo path emitted a <link> for these entries; after this PR they disappear from the HTML entirely, silently disabling DNS-prefetch for affected sites. The PR's own tests only use full URLs, so the regression is not caught.
suggestion: Normalize scheme-less origins to protocol-relative form in the dns-prefetch branch before appending, so bare hostnames survive core's host guard (and produce a valid //host hint).

message: The comment claims the rendered HTML 'stays byte-identical' with the legacy echo path, which is inaccurate. Core normalizes preconnect URLs to scheme+host only (strips paths, query strings, and non-default ports such as https://cdn.example.com:8080), renders dns-prefetch as a protocol-relative //host, and emits single-quoted attributes in a different order (<link href='...' crossorigin='anonymous' rel='preconnect' />). For bare origins with a protocol the href is preserved, but the output is not byte-identical in general.
suggestion: Reword the comment to say the attribute is preserved for functional equivalence rather than byte-identical output, and note that core normalizes preconnect to scheme+host and dns-prefetch to protocol-relative host.

message: The tests only exercise add_resource_hints() in isolation and never simulate core's wp_resource_hints() render loop, so they verify the returned array shape but not the actual behavior the PR promises (crossorigin preservation, URL normalization, and the bare-hostname drop). This is precisely why the dns-prefetch regression went unnoticed.
suggestion: Add a test that feeds the method's return value through a minimal re-implementation of core's render loop (or assert against a simulated normalized output), including a bare-hostname dns-prefetch case and a preconnect URL with a path/port to lock in normalization behavior.

message: Hint emission ordering changes: preconnect/dns-prefetch previously rendered inside add_preload_prefetch_preconnect() at wp_head priority 1 (before the plugin's preload links), but core's wp_resource_hints() runs at priority 2, so the hints now render after the plugin's own preload links. This is cosmetic — browsers treat hint order as irrelevant — but it is an observable HTML change worth noting.
suggestion: No code change required; consider documenting the ordering shift in the method docblock so future maintainers understand why the hints appear after preload links.
